observations.summary: CS-049 is an accepted GUI-facing acceptance contract: save-time validation blocks reserved, malformed, or description-less commands; dry-run renders without launching an agent run; resolved User Commands appear in palette and slash autocomplete.
CS-001 is explicitly retired to migration lineage and is prohibited from re-owning atomized product behavior or creating executable build artifacts.

CS-050 treats duplicate Section 7 headings as a structural anchor defect, requires one canonical anchor, preserves command identifiers and owner references, and forbids semantic changes during repair.
CS-051 reserves `/goal` and `/goal again`, maps them to distinct command IDs, denies User Command override, and keeps Goal Runtime lifecycle semantics outside Commands_System ownership.

CS-052 makes Commands_System an invocation/display consumer while UI_Command_Catalog owns payloads, results, guards, reason codes, receipt effects, idempotency, stale-projection behavior, and recovery routes.
Both visible ledger compile addenda expressly stop at canonical PlanUnits and exclude executable queues, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, and production build tasks.

candidate_findings.summary: CS-049 conditions palette and autocomplete exposure on a command being unresolved and requires a fully resolved dry-run, but it defines neither the unresolved predicate nor failure, feedback, and recovery transitions. Implementations can disagree about when a command disappears, whether save remains allowed, and what preview does when resolution cannot complete.

CS-049 names only plan migration and plan index validators. No acceptance surface exercises blocked save behavior, proves that preview submits no agent run, or asserts palette and autocomplete exposure, so AC-CMD07 through AC-CMD09 can be structurally present without behavioral evidence.

The retired CS-001 bridge contains prescriptive negative-constraint fragments clipped at `redefine it a` and `lock direc`. Even as lineage, these strings do not preserve exact contract meaning, and their active-looking placement leaves consumers uncertain whether to enforce or ignore incomplete obligations.

CS-050 requires one canonical Section 7 anchor and demotion of duplicate heading text but does not select the surviving anchor, specify compatibility aliases or backlink treatment, or define objective manual-review pass conditions. Multiple incompatible repairs could satisfy the stated criteria while changing reference resolution.

The exact `/goal` mappings and nonoverride behavior have no current behavioral validator in CS-051. `future command registry validation` is deferred rather than acceptance evidence, while the only current named surface is plan-index validation.

CS-052 delegates a broad action family to UI_Command_Catalog but declares `depends_on: []` and provides no exact command IDs or contract anchors for those actions. The consumer cannot deterministically bind its invocation and display entries to the semantic owner from this PlanUnit.

CS-052 forbids presets from bypassing owner-defined enablement and stale-projection guards, but its validators cover only plan indexing and ledger validity. No named evidence invokes guarded commands, verifies disabled reasons, or checks receipt and recovery effects.

explicit_non_gaps.summary: The dry-run side-effect boundary is explicit: preview must render without submission to any agent run.
CS-001's intended authority disposition is explicit: it is migration lineage only and must not re-own the atomized source coverage.
Heading repair is explicitly constrained not to rename command identifiers or command-owner references and not to alter command semantics.
The Goal slash-command mapping itself is exact, and both User Commands and `override_builtin` are explicitly denied override authority.
CS-052 clearly assigns UICommand semantics to UI_Command_Catalog and explicitly prohibits Commands_System from redefining schemas or bypassing enablement and stale-projection guards.
The addendum boundaries explicitly exclude implementation and governance generation, so absence of WorkNodes or production build tasks is intentional in this window.

unknowns.summary: The named CS-049 dependencies may define unresolved-state, name-format, and template-resolution semantics, but those PlanUnits are outside this window and were not inspected.
Whether UI_Command_Catalog contains exact IDs, anchors, payloads, result schemas, guards, receipts, and recovery contracts for every CS-052 action cannot be determined from this window.
The window cannot establish whether the deferred command-registry validator has since been implemented elsewhere; CS-051 itself labels it future.
CS-053 begins only in trailing context, so its Teach invocation behavior and acceptance completeness cannot be assessed or promoted to a core finding.
